newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.150 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to up 0.100 cent, livestock analysts said.

Nearby live cattle futures were expected to show strength and deferreds, further weakness following last Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report which showed active marketings and exceptionally large placements. Bull spreading was evident Tuesday following the report and the trend will likely continue. But much of the report is already in the market and deferreds may take their lead from front months, sources said.
Demand in front months of live cattle is also expected to follow the stronger tone to the wholesale beef market and expectations that packers will raise bids for fed cattle soon, analysts said.

Feeder cattle futures appeared oversold Tuesday, as higher corn futures added to pressure from the report and took March down to its lowest level since late December. Prices are seen firming with calls for easier corn futures Tuesday morning also likely to provide support, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.03 at $68.90 per cwt.
